_comment: EVERY DEFECT THE OWNER REPORTS, WITH THE CLOCK RUNNING.
Owner: 'we need to measure how long it takes to fix each problem as we go, so we can
measure our own efficiency ... everything we say should be documented and revisitable
`reported` is when he said it. `fixed` is the COMMIT that fixed it — the elapsed time is
derived from that commit's real author date by tools/log/timeline.mjs, never typed in, so
the number cannot drift from what actually happened. `symptom` is HIS words, kept verbatim,
because his description is the spec and paraphrasing it is how a report gets solved wrong.
An entry with no `fixed` is still open and its age counts against us.

reports.symptom: I'm P1 and I'm trying to fight P2 and it's like P2's not reacting or taking any damage. And I think all of my attacks are hitting myself.
reports.rootCause: A revert on 2026-09-21 deleted resolveHitRegionAtHeight from FrameDataHitbox.ts and left the call to it inside checkCollision. Every connecting strike threw a ReferenceError, so no strike could deal damage on any build carrying it.
reports.howFound: tsc --noEmit named it in one line; CI had been running that check and going red on main for four days.
reports.lesson: A gate that is green somewhere nobody reads is not a gate. Assert the symptom (damage reaches the opponent), not only that it compiles.

reports.symptom: currently can only fire off 4 attack and it's the base ones ... P2's not reacting
reports.rootCause: The game loop clamped dt at 0.05s, so below 20fps every timer in the fight advanced slower than the wall clock. Attacks outlasted the gap between presses: of 16 presses, 10 arrived while the previous move was still running.
reports.howFound: scripts/probe-damage-attribution.mjs — pressed the real keys, counted rising edges, and recorded the fighter's state at each one.
reports.lesson: Measure the CALL COUNT and the STATE at the input, not the code path.

reports.symptom: a lot of character models, GLBs and attires still having stretching and deformation on certain parts of their body
reports.rootCause: JAGER, JAGER_beard and TARZANIAN_DEVIL_skinned were bound ~0.85m from their own skeletons. Bind pose cancels the error exactly, so every existing check vouched for them.
reports.howFound: tools/model_diag/bind_space.mjs — mean distance from a vertex to its dominant joint's bind position, offline over all 77 GLBs.
reports.lesson: A metric that cannot express the failure will vouch for it. skinqa scores a broken rig clean because it asks whether weights predict themselves.

reports.symptom: on Wreck Patterson and Titan they still have parts of their arms attached to parts of their hips and legs ... fix that shit on all the models universally and put in whatever to keep it from ever happening again.
reports.rootCause: OPEN. The weight-level defect is real in the raw assets (WRECK_PATTERSON 180 bleeding verts, TITAN 136, worst pairs Hips~RightArm / Hips~LeftForeArm) and the load-time prune clears it completely (4/4 clean after the pipeline). The visible stretching is a separate thing: the share of the body bound to a DISTANT bone (WRECK 5.60%, godwithin 5.49%, TITAN 2.25%, VIPER — never reported — 0.33%).
reports.attempted: A load-time repair rebinding far-bound vertices to the nearest bone SEGMENT. MEASURED WORSE and reverted: same probe, same clip, VIPER's stretch share went 3.21% -> 4.17% and WRECK's 2.14% -> 3.90%, because rebinding only the outliers leaves a seam against their untouched neighbours.
reports.lesson: THREE INDEPENDENT MEASUREMENTS NOW SAY THE WEIGHTS ARE CLEAN, and one of my own earlier numbers was wrong. (1) The live scene: scripts/probe-live-skin.mjs walks the RENDERED bodies in a real WRECK vs TITAN match and counts 0 bleeding vertices on both (12,035 and 11,469 verts), so the load-time prune reaches the screen, not just the test harness. (2) Bone-segment distance: WRECK's median is 16.9cm against VIPER's 17.1cm — indistinguishable from a model never complained about. (3) My earlier 'WRECK 5.60% vs VIPER 0.33% far-bound' was an ARTIFACT of measuring distance to the joint ORIGIN; a joint sits at one END of its bone, so an ankle vertex is legitimately 0.4m from the knee that drives it, and the 'defect' was almost entirely legs. That also explains why the rebind repair made stretching worse: it was moving correctly-weighted vertices. Posed stretching does remain, on EVERY model including ones never reported (VIPER's worst edge growth is larger than WRECK's), so whatever is visible in the screenshots is not cross-body skin weights and needs the owner to point at the exact body part, or a look at the rendering side rather than the rig.

reports.symptom: pull in any open source so you can actually see and test and play ... pull stuff from open source that'll get our fights actually going well
reports.rootCause: The Quaternius Universal Animation Library (CC0-1.0, commercially safe) was fetched, unpacked and listed in OpenAnimationSources.generated.ts, and contributed ZERO clips. Two bugs: the bake filtered files with /\\.glb$/ — a regex requiring a literal BACKSLASH before the extension, which no POSIX path has, so nothing matched and it reported zero skips and zero errors; and once found, every clip failed the SkeletonUtils cross-check because three's retargetClip reads target.skeleton.bones unconditionally and the canonical target is a bare bone tree.
reports.howFound: The bake report said quaterniusSources: 0 while three GLBs sat in vendor/. A silent 100% loss with no skip and no error recorded.
reports.lesson: A pipeline that reports zero skips AND zero output is not idle, it is broken. Count what went IN, not just what came out.

reports.symptom: combat is a bit smoother, but it's still not on the level of Tekken ... I can tell you're still hand tooling things when I told you to pull in open source for these fixes ... actually pull stuff from [the Schwarzerblitz repo]
reports.rootCause: Attack displacement came from ATTACK_ROOT_MOTION_PROFILES, a hand-written table of FIVE entries keyed by animation name, while the imported Schwarzerblitz move graph carries authored per-frame root motion on 127 of its 133 moves that nothing read. The importer also discarded the '>' interpolation flag (165 of 169 movement lines carry it), so every authored travel would have been read as a single-frame teleport. Root motion was also armed for P1 only — the opponent never travelled with an attack at all.
reports.howFound: Counted engine consumption of every field in the imported graph: hidden 0, animationRightSide 0, range 0, newStance 0, movement 0. Semantics then read out of the Schwarzerblitz C++ (FK_Move, FK_MoveFileParser, FK_Character) rather than guessed.
reports.lesson: RESOLVED UNIVERSALLY. Two independent sources of travel existed and neither reached the game: Schwarzerblitz authors it in #MOVEMENT (its animations are rotation-only by design), and our own captures perform it in a `pose` block of joint world positions that nothing read — 273 of 973 source clips travel more than 15cm, up to 1.22m. Both now feed ONE cumulative travel curve (src/engine/motion/RootTravel.ts) sampled between two instants, so it is frame-rate independent by construction. Read at BAKE time from public/motion, so every future clip gets it by existing rather than by somebody remembering to wire it up. Orientation comes from the shoulder axis and is pinned by a test against moves whose names state their direction (BackStep negative, DROP_KICK positive), because an inverted sign keeps every magnitude believable and only shows up as fighters retreating when they attack.

reports.symptom: when you press back and attack, it's like kind of doing something where it's making you keep walking back. So when you do back and attack, none of those attacks ever hit. In Tekken and Schwarzerblitz it's more specific than that.
reports.rootCause: NOT the attack carrying you — measured strictly between the start and end of the attack, movement is 0.000m on every input including back, so the state machine anchors you correctly. The fighter walked OUT OF RANGE before the attack's active frames arrived. Scale-free comparison: Schwarzerblitz crosses 1.23 of its own strike reaches per second of walking (80 units/s over a 65-unit modal range); we crossed 1.57 (2.2 m/s over a MEASURED 1.40m reach).
reports.howFound: scripts/audit-combat-feel.mjs — real presses in a real match, measuring displacement, connection and the move that fired per input.
reports.lesson: TWO OF MY OWN READINGS WERE WRONG BEFORE THE RIGHT ONE. First I timed drift over a fixed window around the press and reported 1.76m of 'the attack carrying you' — most of it was legitimate walking, because holding back is supposed to walk you back. Then I took the strike reach as 0.8m from the distance another test happened to swing at, which made the pace gap look like 2.2x and produced a 1.0 m/s walk that was sluggish rather than deliberate. Driving every attack out to its furthest connecting distance says all four reach 1.40m and the real gap was 1.28x. MEASURE THE THING, INCLUDING THE DENOMINATOR.

reports.symptom: we need to pull more stuff from Tekken and Schwarzerblitz ... so it feels like something built on top of Tekken and classic fighting games
reports.rootCause: 50 imported moves declare the stance they END in (#NEWSTANCE) and nothing read it. Stance was derived from the pad every frame — Crouch while you hold down, Ground the instant you release — so a move could never LEAVE you anywhere. That made the genre's whole grounded/rising/wake-up layer unreachable: Ukemi (breakfall to standing), SupineReversal (up off your back), sweeps that end crouching, dashes that end running.
reports.howFound: tools/audit/unconsumed_fields.mjs — the consumption gate built after the same shape of bug appeared three times. SbMove.newStance was in its baseline as a named gap, and dropped off the report on its own once the field had a reader.
reports.lesson: A move-imposed stance must survive a NEUTRAL pad but yield to a deliberate input, or it is a trap rather than a position. And the first version of the test called the state machine without attaching a command buffer, so the special could never match, a bare press fell through to the DEFAULT light attack (which carries no end stance), and a correct implementation looked broken. The test now asserts the move under test actually ran.

reports.symptom: the combat needs to be more ... so it feels like something built on top of Tekken and classic fighting games ... we really need to research and pull from code and stuff in those games to get a better flow going
reports.rootCause: NO MOVE A PLAYER FIRES COULD BE CANCELLED. detectCancel reads cancelInto/followups off the current move; the 26 generated directional slots carried neither, and neither do the four DEFAULT_MOVE_WINDOWS. So every attack ran to completion: throw one, sit through its whole recovery, throw the next. That is the difference between a fighting game and a sequence of single hits.
reports.howFound: Checked whether the moves the player actually fires carry the cancel data the source authors — the same 'imported but never read' shape that has now appeared four times this session.
reports.lesson: The WINDOW SHAPE is measured (213 authored windows across 133 imported moves open at a median 0.20 of the move) but the PAIRING is a derived default, because the source authors named strings per move and generated slots have none. Same direction, other button — punch into kick and back. One link, not a licence to cancel into anything, so it cannot become a mash.

reports.symptom: ours are keyed by destination rather than by from->to pair — worth doing. And get all fixed and bugs with model stretching tearing and ugly unblended animations ... fixed so we have a better game base
reports.rootCause: FADE_DURATIONS was keyed only by the destination state, so a snap out of a hit reaction and a long settle out of a run got the same duration entering the same idle. Measured over 714 real clip transitions, the pose distance between them spans 20 to 68 degrees — a spread one key cannot express.
reports.howFound: Read the Namco Cancel struct in Kiloutre/TKMovesets (cloned, not paraphrased) and measured our own corpus's transition distances.
reports.lesson: COMPUTED BEATS TABULATED when the table would be 200,000 invented cells. The distance is already knowable from the live skeleton against the incoming clip's first frame. TWO THINGS CHECKED AND FOUND NOT TO APPLY: the Lerp-vs-Slerp diagnosis (1,570 hemisphere flips exist, but every interpolation here goes through THREE.Quaternion.slerp which corrects the sign, and there are no raw quaternion lerps) and LBS candy-wrapping (not yet measured — the remaining posed stretching is present on every model including ones never reported). STILL OPEN from the reference: Tekken's Cancel carries `starting_frame`, the frame the TARGET move begins at when cancelled into, which lets a string's second hit flow instead of replaying its startup. We have no data to fill it.

reports.symptom: A punch should not cause a 90-degree pelvic torsion ... The Structural Fix: Bone Masking. Also: Gemini keeps talking about c++ idk how to permanently correct it from assuming.
reports.rootCause: He was describing the clips, not the skinning. Measured on the shipped ALTERNATINGFOREARMS, the pelvis rotates away from its own first frame through 0 10 11 30 33 32 46 71 100 84 40 10 38 76 103 102 112 111 101 121 108 105 101 101 — it peaks at 121 degrees and ENDS 101 out. CHOKESLAM ends 117 out, DDT 86. Against the real IDLE stance a hand strike put the pelvis 94.6 degrees outside anywhere the fighter stands. 190 of 455 clips carry a lower body that is either faster than the bank's own fastest real kick (HURRICANE_KICK, 786 deg/s) or never returns the pelvis to a stance.
reports.howFound: Measured per frame rather than reasoning about it. The first attempt at a tagging rule — a large leg offset that barely varies is a baked-in constant — was measured and REJECTED: it tags 126 clips and puts ALTERNATINGFOREARMS in the safe pile, because its legs travel 174 degrees, which reads as footwork until you see it travelled at 998 deg/s.
reports.lesson: DO NOT MEASURE CORRUPT DATA TO DECIDE WHETHER TO TRUST IT — that is circular. The engine already knows something better: what the player pressed. A jab is a jab whatever its capture contains, so the mask comes from the motion state and the measurement is the evidence and the gate instead. SECOND LESSON, mine: a stance is an ENVELOPE, not a pose. Comparing the held pelvis with ONE frame of IDLE reported 64.5 degrees with the mask working perfectly, because IDLE's own pelvis sways 55 degrees over its cycle. THIRD: three.js has no per-bone pose-evaluation loop to skip inside, so a bone mask is a TRACK SPLIT plus a second action — the mixer accumulates per binding, so a bone with no track in any playing action is simply never written. 94.6 degrees outside the stance -> 7.2, with the same clip played as a kick as the in-run control.

reports.symptom: the animations being in the wrong spot, like I'm still noticing where if I press forward and kick, that it's crouching and doing a kick when that should be at the down and kick
reports.rootCause: Two halves, both real. (1) attack_lk led with DROP_KICK, the first alias present in the bake, so it WAS the light kick for every character: spineUp 0.655, a body leaning about 49 degrees off vertical, and 2.900s long. CROUCHINGKICK, one place further down the same list, measures 0.507 and is the genuinely crouched clip — exactly where he said it belonged. (2) crouchLightAttack and crouchHeavyAttack have had frame data since MoveLibrary was written and NOTHING in FighterStateMachine ever entered either one: the standing attack checks came first and matched on the button alone, so a crouching player pressing kick got the standing kick. Their semantics pointed at standing clips too (crouchLightAttack -> attack_1, the standing jab). THE GATE WRITTEN FOR IT THEN FOUND THE SAME DEFECT ON ALL FOUR BASIC ATTACKS: attack_1 played BOXING at 1.733s striking BACKWARD (fwd -0.999), attack_rp played COMBO_PUNCH at 2.967s (fwd -1.000), attack_rk played HURRICANE_KICK at 1.833s, which this file already recorded as a frozen capture that 'plays as a spinning statue'.
reports.howFound: The existing uprightness gate is UPRIGHT_SPINE_MIN = 0, which only catches a body that is fully inverted, so 0.655 sailed through. The new bar is 0.85 plus a 1.6s ceiling, applied to what each slot ACTUALLY RESOLVES TO rather than to every alias, and it caught three more slots the moment it existed.
reports.lesson: A GATE SET TO CATCH THE CATASTROPHE MISSES THE DEFECT. Zero only rejects a body that is upside down; the thing that was shipping was a body leaning 49 degrees, which looks exactly like the crouch the owner reported. SECOND: the replacements were chosen only from each slot's OWN curated list. Ranked over all 455 clips for 'upright, forward-striking, short', the best hand strikes are ELENATHROWREACTION, TIGERSTANCE and MIRAAIRTHROWREACTION — two hit reactions and a stance. No measurement in this repo can tell an attack from a body being thrown, which is precisely why the move-library checkboxes exist, and sweeping the bake would have put a hit reaction on the jab. THIRD: the file itself had recorded HURRICANE_KICK as a spinning statue and left it leading because reordering was 'a design decision' — a known defect parked behind a decision nobody was going to come back and make. The gate is what forces the decision.

reports.symptom: there's still this issue with the little hit effects ... staying on screen for too long, and the fighter not reacting
reports.rootCause: They were not lingering, they were NEVER EXPIRING. Two defects on either side of the same seam. (1) The rAF loop in CombatArena3D declared `tick`, registered a cleanup and NEVER SCHEDULED THE FIRST FRAME — the effect body ran to its return and that was that, so the loop has never run once. The only thing that ever advanced the pool was a one-shot requestAnimationFrame at each of the four spawn sites, each of which ticked exactly once and never re-armed: an orb spawned with 0.35s of life lost 1/60 of it and then sat there until the next hit happened to tick it again, so it took roughly 21 more hits to clear one orb. (2) tickHitEffectPool subtracted a hardcoded 1/60 per call while being driven off rAF, so even with the loop alive an effect's real lifetime was authored * (60 / actual fps) — double on a 30fps phone, triple at 20. The point light, the camera shake and the screen flash all decayed per CALL for the same reason.
reports.howFound: Read the loop rather than the effect. The giveaway was four separate one-shot rAFs all writing the same ref — nobody writes that next to a working self-arming loop.
reports.lesson: THE THIRD TIME THIS EXACT SHAPE HAS COME UP IN ONE SESSION: a system written, complete, and never called. Before tuning a duration, check that the thing which spends it runs at all — and count how many times, because once is a number that looks like working. The other half is the same fixed-timestep defect already fixed in FighterStateMachine, one system along: anything holding a value in SECONDS must be spent in seconds, and anything holding it in 60fps FRAMES must be spent at dt*60. A per-call decay is a frame-rate-dependent decay.

reports.symptom: Keep working and check groks new work and merge in. Grok new work on https://github.com/mhvnsnt/brutalfist11 too
reports.rootCause: Two sources. rocket-update (4 commits from 2026-09-18) converts the build from Vite to Next.js, cuts the test script from ~30 files to 6, drops the register-ts-resolve loader every TS test needs, removes the --gate bake from predev/prebuild and deletes vite.config.ts, the PWA service worker, tools/model_diag/bind_pose.mjs, tools/tekken, tools/posesheet and tools/skinbleed — 4.5M insertions across 1174 files with main not an ancestor. brutalfist11 is a single-commit export that ALREADY CONTAINS today's work, so it is a clean superset: Tekken guard resolution, stick-dies-on-startup, zstd motion (11MB -> 3MB), asset streaming, meshopt models (-10.2MB), a typography pass and the first-tap fix.
reports.howFound: Read every shared file's diff rather than merging wholesale, and judged each asset class with a measurement instead of a file size.
reports.lesson: FIVE THINGS WOULD HAVE COME IN SILENTLY. (1) rocket-update's Next.js conversion and tool deletions — its one real finding, the React peer conflict, was taken as a CONSTRAINT rather than its override. (2) grok-pwa-shared.mjs reverting a documented subdirectory-build fix. (3) MAIME_skinned and MAIME_tattered_skinned with TEXCOORD_0 pruned, seams 2954->0 — his face paint is assigned at runtime and a pruner cannot see that. (4) The momentum chip silently killed: chipDamageMultiplier left set and read by nobody, which is exactly what the unconsumed-fields gate is for. (5) bf11's re-bake, which the credibility gate scored WORSE on 12 of 18 differing clips (HIT_TO_BODY 289 -> 3021 deg/s). AND TWO THINGS GROK WROTE THAT HAD NEVER RUN: tekken-guard.test.ts and tekken-commit.test.ts were never added to the test script, and meshoptDecoderShim.ts had zero callers while installAssetStream's own header claimed the alias was in place. Grep for callers on every new file in a merge, and register every new test.

reports.symptom: find out like the full umbrella term that will audit everything in this versus something like Tekken 7 so we can get everything that's not good baseline in our game ... whether it be gameplay combat animation or whatever ... it's taking way too long to fix and hand tool this when we can start with a good base start and I keep saying that with so many of my projects but it's like you're ignoring me just to play around and experiment and hand tool everything anyway.
reports.rootCause: He is right that there was no baseline to measure against, so every fix was chosen by whatever was most recently visible rather than by what was furthest from playable. The umbrella is SYSTEM MECHANICS MEASURED IN FRAME DATA — the only part of a fighting game that is objectively comparable between two titles. Six axes: TIMEBASE, FRAME DATA, MECHANICS, INPUT, ANIMATION, FEEL. First run: 76% across 36 rows. The biggest gap was advantage on block — blockstun was a flat per-animation duration never compared against the attacker's recovery, so EVERY move was neutral and there was no reason to press after one move and wait after another. Also measured: the light punch was 7.2 frames of startup against the i10 lineage standard, too FAST rather than too slow.
reports.howFound: Built the audit before fixing anything else, and made it score DECLARED as zero — this project's recurring failure is a system that exists and is never called, so 'we have it' does not count.
reports.lesson: A BASELINE IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OPINION, and the three verdicts are what make it useful: BEHAVING (a measured value in range, under a registered test), WIRED (called but unproven), DECLARED (exists, nothing calls it). DECLARED scores nothing, because BANNON_TAG, crouchLightAttack, meshoptDecoderShim, the hit-effect rAF loop and two Tekken tests in this week's merge were all 'present' and all dead. Every gap row names the open source to fill it from — Kiloutre/TKMovesets, SchwarzerblitzEngine, CMU/Truebones/Mixamo — so the next pass is an import rather than another hand-rolled system. 76% -> 79% in one change by deriving blockstun from an authored advantage instead of authoring both independently.

reports.symptom: pull in rage and low parry and other combat and animations and blending and etc gaps from open source
reports.rootCause: Two of the three gaps were not missing code, they were unread code. RAGE already existed as `Finisher` in OverdriveSystem — FINISHER_HP_THRESHOLD 0.25, FINISHER_DAMAGE 350, FINISHER_STARTUP_FRAMES 15 described as 'super armor startup', which is a Rage Art — and those constants, plus HEAT_ATTACKS and SUPER_ARMOR_ACTIVE_FRAMES, had zero readers outside their own file. The arena gated the finisher HUD on a literal 0.25. And WALL_SPLAT_BONUS_FRAMES (18, 'extra frames attacker gets to chain combo') was written into every wall splat by applyWallSplat and read by nobody, so a wall carry bought no frames. Low parry was genuinely absent — only the word appeared.
reports.howFound: Cloned and read SchwarzerblitzEngine rather than designing from memory. Its `FK_Character::hasArmor(type)` asks the MOVE, at the CURRENT FRAME, about a SPECIFIC ATTACK TYPE, with windows on the move (FK_Move armorFrames / invincibilityFrames) and coverage as an attack-type bitmask with composite masks. That one shape collapses power crush, Rage Art invincibility and low parry into a single mechanism.
reports.lesson: PROBE THE SYSTEM, NOT THE WORD — the audit searched 'Rage|rage' and called it missing while a complete implementation sat under another name. Same error as classifying a move by its filename. SECOND: copying the reference's SHAPE is worth more than copying its features. Per-frame, per-attack-height windows meant a power crush became one line on the heavy punch instead of a fourth half-system beside the three that already existed. THIRD, from the reference's own first line — `if (isBeingThrown()) return false;` — a throw beats armour, and that is what keeps armour from being a free win. FOURTH, mine: a window starting at frame 1 leaves a move unarmoured on the frame it comes out, which is when a trade is most likely; the resolver's unit test had asserted frame 0 was closed and driving the real state machine caught it. 79% -> 89% of baseline, 0 declared-and-dead rows.

reports.symptom: pull in rage and low parry and other combat and animations and blending and etc gaps from open source
reports.rootCause: The ANIMATION axis read 100% on four thin rows. Probed against what modern open-source locomotion actually does, we had NONE of foot IK/locking, inertialisation, turn-in-place, stride/distance matching, or motion matching. The measurable one is foot sliding: every locomotion clip has zero hips travel because root motion is neutralised and the engine translates the root, so the stride is the clip's while the speed is the engine's. Measured by FK on the planted foot — GINGA_BACKWARD authored at 2.492 m/s and played while moving at 1.72 (sliding 0.77 m/s), DRUNK_RUN_FORWARD authored at 3.277 and played at 4.30 (sliding 1.02). The forward walk was nearly right by luck at 1.839 vs 1.72.
reports.howFound: Probed for the features by name first and got nothing, then measured the one that has a number: authored stride speed against engine speed. TPOSE reading 0.000 m/s is the control that says the FK measurement works.
reports.lesson: AN AUDIT THAT ONLY ASKS EASY QUESTIONS SCORES WELL. Adding three real animation rows took the baseline from 92% of 36 rows to 87% of 39, and two came back MISSING — the audit got more truthful and the game did not get worse. The gate now holds 0-declared-and-dead as the figure that must never regress, because the percentage moves whenever the question set improves. AND: FighterMesh is the live animation path and does not use buildAnimationController, so wiring the playback rate into the controller alone would have been dead code — the same trap this file has recorded four times. Foot IK and turn-in-place are left MISSING with the reason stated: the stage is flat, and a fighting game holds facing to the opponent.
